title: One image, thousands of cache entries
description: An image origin uses w and h query parameters to resize images. Marketing links also include a unique utm_source value that never changes the image. Your CDN keys on the entire URL, so identical images rarely share a cache entry. What cache-key rule improves reuse without mixing different image sizes?

options.text: Keep normalized host, path, w and h in the key; omit the confirmed tracking-only parameter.
options.explanation: The key still distinguishes response-changing variants, while tracking values no longer create duplicate cached bodies. The rule depends on knowing which inputs the origin actually uses.

options.text: Ignore all query parameters and cache by path alone.
options.explanation: That improves reuse by returning the wrong dimensions to some visitors. Cache correctness comes before hit ratio.

options.text: Add the full User-Agent header to the existing key.
options.explanation: That introduces more variants without removing tracking-only ones. It further fragments the cache unless the response truly depends on that header.

options.text: Keep the key unchanged and increase the origin's default TTL.
options.explanation: A longer TTL retains each fragmented copy longer, but new tracking values still produce misses.
